hero.intro: Spaces with attitude. We design interiors and furniture that unite function and calm.

studio.title: One studio, one point of contact, one standard.
studio.text: Studio von Boros is my practice for interior architecture and bespoke furniture in Berlin. I plan, draw and oversee the build myself — from the first measurement to the mounted front. The focus is the untapped potential of urban apartments: considered built-ins, honest materials, and spaces that make everyday life easier.

about.title: Daniel von Boros
about.lead: Architect in Berlin. I design interiors, built-ins and bespoke furniture, and see them through to the mounted front.

sections.title: From the whole to the detail
sections.text: I studied architecture and bring more than 5 years of professional experience as an architect with me. One habit I developed: I think about a space as a whole before I draw the first piece of furniture. Proportion before decoration.

sections.title: A detour through software
sections.text: After that I spent three years as a software developer. It taught me to structure processes clearly and to record decisions precisely. My plans benefit from it today: unambiguous, complete, buildable.

sections.title: One studio, one point of contact
sections.text: Studio von Boros is deliberately small. I plan, draw and oversee the build myself, from the first measurement to the mounted front. For wood and metal work I collaborate with a partner workshop that builds from my detail drawings. One person stays responsible, from the first line to the last joint.

sections.title: What I work on
sections.text: My focus is Berlin's period and loft apartments: high ceilings, alcoves, walk-through rooms, spaces that should do more than they do today. Typical tasks are a home office in an alcove, a room divider between living and sleeping, a loft bed with desk and storage, or a material and colour concept for the whole apartment.

sections.title: What I care about
sections.text: An intervention should not look like a renovation, but as if it had always been that way. That is why I work with honest materials, calm proportions and the light that is already there.

items.q: Who does Studio von Boros work for?
items.a: Mainly for owners of period and loft apartments in Berlin who want to develop their spaces with a design-led approach. It is less about quickly solving a lack of space and more about an intervention that looks as if it had always been there.

items.q: Does Studio von Boros design built-in wardrobes and bespoke furniture?
items.a: Yes, built-ins and bespoke furniture are the core of my work: built-in wardrobes, wall units, room dividers, alcove solutions and individual pieces such as sideboards. I design them to suit the room and its existing fabric, draw the detail plans and oversee production through to installation.

items.q: Are interior architecture and furniture design available from a single source?
items.a: Yes. Room concept, floor plan, built-ins, furniture, material and colour concept and detail plans all come from one studio. There is one point of contact from the first measurement to the mounted front. Production takes place to my plans in a partner workshop for wood and metal.

items.q: Which materials does Studio von Boros work with?
items.a: With materials that show what they are and may gain a patina over time: wood such as oak, matt lacquered surfaces, glass, mirror and metals such as brass. In period apartments, floorboards, stucco and high ceilings are part of the material. I plan with them, not against them.

items.q: How much does the planning cost?
items.a: The room concept costs from €2,400 per room at a fixed price. It includes the initial consultation and on-site measurement in Berlin, a room concept with floor plan and furnishings, the design of built-ins and bespoke furniture, a material and colour concept and detail plans for implementation. Complete apartments and multiple rooms are planned on an individual quote. Production is not included; its cost depends on size, material and finish.

It starts with an initial consultation and on-site measurement. This leads to the room concept with floor plan and furnishings, followed by the design of the built-ins with a material and colour concept. The detail plans go into production; on request I oversee the work through to installation.

items.q: Who is behind Studio von Boros?
items.a: Daniel von Boros, architect in Berlin, registered with the Berlin Chamber of Architects. The studio is based in Berlin-Schöneberg; appointments take place across Berlin by arrangement.
